fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Open Terrain; Long Driveway
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from both directions on the street.
• Install reflective markers or posts along both sides of the driveway to guide responders at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the full width of the driveway clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responders can reach the residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible address or unit identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence on arrival.
• Identify and mark a turnaround area near the residence so that fire apparatus and emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Keep the area around the detached structure accessible by maintaining a clear path from the driveway to its entry points.
• Post the street address at the end of the driveway at street level so it is readable from a moving vehicle.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Single Access Route; Large Trees; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Tall Grass Area; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Mow or cut the tall grass area down before fire season and keep it short throughout the dry months.
• Trim shrubs that are within close range of the structure to create open space between the plants and the building.
• Remove dry or dead grass buildup near the base of scattered shrubs close to the house.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Cut back low branches on large trees near the house to raise the canopy off the ground.
• Keep grass mowed short along both sides of the driveway so it does not carry fire toward the house.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over or crowd the driveway to keep the route open for vehicles.
• Since there is only one way in and out, keep the driveway clear of fallen branches, overgrown brush, and tall grass at all times.
• Remove dead grass and dry plant material that has built up around the base of large trees near the house.
• Keep the open terrain areas between trees and shrubs free of tall grass to limit how fire can move across the property.
